item.title: Nara Park and Its Sacred Deer: Meeting the Bowing Deer — Guide
item.description: Nara Park is a vast green expanse at the heart of the old capital, home to Todaiji, Kasuga Taisha and Kofukuji — and to over a thousand wild sika deer that wander freely among the temples and lawns. Revered for centuries as sacred messengers of the gods of Kasuga Shrine and now designated a natural treasure, the deer are Nara’s most beloved sight: gentle, bold and famous for bowing their heads to request the shika-senbei crackers sold at stalls throughout the park.
